rationale:
features_open/030 §10 v2(d). A finding from the offer-analyser carries its own acceptance test as PROSE, and nothing checks it mechanically. This adds an OPTIONAL, per-finding structured predicate alongside the prose, plus the deterministic gate that decides whether one may be stored.

WHY, MEASURED. [MEASURED 2026-08-24, live clients_db + served pages] of the 37 acceptance tests this agent has written, THREE sit on work items marked complete - page rebuilt, deployed, commit_sha in the item result - while their own stated criterion is refuted by a one-line check over the exact field the test itself names. Worked case: webdesign.co.uk/index, item created 08-24 10:13Z and completed 10:34Z, test "the meta description must state the zero-data or zero-account promise BEFORE any catalogue count", served meta_description "Sixty-three browser tools for web design and development. No account, no upload, everything runs in your browser." The served meta tag was fetched and is byte-identical to pages.meta_description. Second: the same page, same clause, an 08-22 item, also complete. Third: robot-hands.com/gripper-catalog-index, "appears as a clickable link in the site header navigation", absent from the served header, item complete. A fourth (webdesign/about, "must not contain curated" against a meta opening "Curated guides...") is refuted at wont_fix, so it is not a false green.

THE DESIGN IS TWO RULES, and they are the answer to the trap features_open/030 states against this very feature ("a plausible predicate over a judgement clause grades confidently and wrongly - worse than the prose it replaced, because it carries a green tick"):
(1) REFUTE-ONLY. A predicate is a NECESSARY condition of the prose test, never sufficient. Satisfying it means "not refuted" and never "the test is met"; the prose stays the authority. Two thirds of the live corpus welds a checkable clause to a judgement clause.
(2) IT MUST REFUTE AT EMISSION OR IT IS DISCARDED. The finding asserts the page is wrong today, so a condition that genuinely expresses it must fail today. This is the ONLY property of a predicate checkable at the moment it is written, and it excludes the vacuous case - a needle present nowhere, a clause already satisfied - which would otherwise be stored as honesty machinery and grade green for ever. This is deliberately strict and it does throw away useful-but-currently-satisfied conditions; the trade is taken on bugs_closed/335, where from_field - a field built to prove sourcing - vouched for a number the cited premise never contained. A predicate is the same kind of self-attributing artefact, and the only version we can PROVE is coupled to the finding in front of us is one that fails in front of us. Discards are recorded per finding under acceptance_predicate_rejected, never dropped silently.

VOCABULARY DERIVED FROM THE CORPUS, NOT INVENTED: three text shapes (text_absent, text_present with min, text_order) over exactly two fields (pages.meta_description, pages.title) of one named page. text_order accepts the reserved needle $cardinal, resolved through CLM-023's existing word-aware scanner, because "...before any count of tools" is the commonest ordering clause in the corpus and names no string.

REUSE, stated because same-package helpers never appear in a diff: digitCardinalSpans, cardinalPointWordRe and cardinalUnits are PRE-EXISTING in verify_cited_cardinals_action.go (CLM-023, live on v1.0.1332). The only change to that file is extracting the letter-adjacency loop out of digitCardinalsIn into digitCardinalSpans, so the new file can ask WHERE the first quantity is rather than which quantities exist. Behaviour is unchanged and its 18 existing tests - three written specifically for that rule (B2B/S3/IPv6, real quantities, hyphenated model names) - are the proof; no test file was touched. pageNameAliases is likewise pre-existing in write_audit_findings_action.go and is reused so the gate resolves "homepage" exactly as the write does.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT REUSE, and why: the existing criteria-fence vocabulary (selector_exists / attribute_matches / has_visible_area in experience_criteria.go, offered to this lane by the staged-component-build lane in CONTRIB_2026-08-04). It is DOM-shaped and browser-evaluated. This population is page METADATA served in the head, and the checkable clause is text arithmetic over one string: nothing here needs a browser, a fence or a tier.

WHY NAV IS NOT IN THE VOCABULARY, although 3 of the 37 tests are about the header: because the obvious source is wrong and fails toward a CONFIDENT FALSE REFUTATION. [MEASURED 2026-08-24] leopardessconsulting.co.uk has 13 pages with pages.in_header=true; its served header renders 7 destinations. A predicate reading the column would have refuted "the header nav contains no more than seven items" - a test that HOLDS at the artefact. I hit this while measuring, before writing any code. pages.rendered_header, which looks like the escape route, is empty on all 35 active pages of robot-hands.com.

BLAST RADIUS, named rather than left to the reviewer. write_audit_findings is a SHARED action with many producers (design-audit, render-audit, tool-acceptance, this one). Its change is two optional struct fields and two conditional spec keys, absent by default: a producer whose workflow does not carry the new gate step can never populate them, and its spec is byte-identical to today. That is the 2026-08-02 opt-in-with-the-unsafe-side-off shape. Consumers read spec keys by name, so an added key is inert; the only key-set-sensitive reader is cmd/verifier-remit-check, whose family-overlap threshold is 0.5 and which would see 11/12 = 0.917 overlap, and whose census is a frozen 2026-08-11 fixture rather than a live assertion.

TWO CORRECTNESS TRAPS I HAD TO HANDLE, both in write_audit_findings existing code:
(a) parseAuditFindings third return (shapeRecognised) arms silence retraction: a RECOGNISED empty findings list is read as "the auditor found nothing" and retracts prior findings (bugs_open/213 D1 half two). An unresolvable findings path is NOT that statement, so the gate omits the findings key entirely in that case, which leaves write_audit_findings on exactly the nil branch it takes today - zero items, no retraction - while a genuinely empty array is passed through AS an empty array. Two tests hold both directions.
(b) write_audit_findings decodes findings TWICE - struct tags for a JSON string, a hand-written map in findingsFromList for a native list - and the native list is the shape an upstream ACTION hands over, i.e. the only path this feature uses. A field added to the struct and forgotten there is dropped in SILENCE. Both are updated, and held by a reflection test that walks the struct json tags.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated so it cannot be written up as more: nothing automated reads acceptance_predicate yet, so TODAY IT PREVENTS NO FALSE GREEN - it makes one machine-checkable. The consumer this unblocks is a COMPLETION-time check beside complete_work_item_no_change.go, whose own comment records that grading acceptance_test needs a producer-side contract change first; the evaluator is therefore exported (EvaluateAcceptancePredicate) with no dependence on ActionParams or a DB handle, so that consumer is a call and not a rewrite. It is NOT built here: it would change live completion semantics for a shared handler and deserves its own round. That leaves the same residual as CLM-023's drop record - a record with no automated consumer - and the register entry states it as a precondition on the next change, in the ACTION rather than in one call site, per the bug_historian seat ruling on 335.

PATHS THIS RATIONALE MENTIONS THAT ARE NOT IN THE EDIT LIST, one clause each (per the editquality lesson that an objection naming one file is naming a CATEGORY): 601_offer_analyser_acceptance_predicates_HOLD_ROLLBACK.sql EXISTS, is written, and is omitted because council scope refuses _ROLLBACK sidecars client-side, so listing it would spend the round without ever showing a reviewer the file; docs/agent_docs/docs026_concept_register/register/claims-verification.md and 000_concept_index.md carry the CLM-024 entry REQUIRED IN THE SAME COMMIT by the 2026-07-28 seam ruling, are written, and are omitted for the identical client-side reason (prose); the lane docs and features_open/030 are prose, same reason; experience_criteria.go, complete_work_item_no_change.go and cmd/verifier-remit-check are cited as EVIDENCE and are not edited - nothing in them changes.

plan.summary: features_open/030 v2(d): a finding may carry a refute-only, machine-checkable half of its own acceptance test, kept only where it already refutes the page
plan.risks: The vocabulary is narrow by design, so most findings will carry no predicate and adoption may be ZERO on the first run - the safe direction (the key is deliberately absent from the OUTPUT skeleton) and measurable, but it means this may deliver nothing until the completion-time consumer exists. Rule 2 (must refute at emission) discards necessary conditions that already hold, which are not worthless: a later rewrite could break one. Accepted on 335 evidence, and the rejection record makes the cost countable rather than invisible. The predicate is evaluated over the FULL pages.meta_description while the model authored it against a value truncated at 160 chars in the offer surface, so a needle past char 160 is visible to the gate and was not visible to its author. write_audit_findings is shared: the passthrough is absent-by-default and inert for other producers, but it is a key added to a spec many consumers read by name. The migration must not be applied before an image carrying the action rolls, which is why it is _HOLD; applied early it does not degrade, it rejects the whole workflow.

edits.rationale: The new gate action plus the exported evaluator. The decision points: EvaluateAcceptancePredicate returns the VERDICT (refutes / holds / inapplicable) and the action decides what is STORED - rule 2 lives in that if. The vocabulary tables are closed maps, so an unknown type or a key no checker reads REJECTS rather than being ignored (the P7 rule borrowed from experience_criteria.go). Config is site_id + findings_field and nothing else, deliberately.

26 tests. Every corpus string is REAL, read from the live estate on 2026-08-24, because the design question is how the model actually writes and what the pages actually say - it cannot be answered from invented examples. The two load-bearing tests are the ones an obvious implementation FAILS: the word-boundary false refutation (with a positive control and an assertion that the substring is genuinely there, so the premise cannot rot) and the vacuous predicate. The only invented string is a MUTATION of the live one - the same clauses reordered, i.e. what the demanded fix looks like - which proves the gate can be turned off by the repair it asks for.

The ONLY change to the live CLM-023 gate: the letter-adjacency loop is extracted out of digitCardinalsIn into digitCardinalSpans so the new file can ask WHERE the first quantity is instead of which quantities exist. digitCardinalsIn now calls it and maps spans to normalised values - same regex, same rejection rule, same output. A second copy of that rule was the alternative and it would drift: each clause was paid for by a live defect (B2B->2, S3->3, IPv6->6, found on the gate first two production runs). The 18 existing tests are the proof, three of them written specifically for this rule, and no test file was touched.

The passthrough on the SHARED write: two optional struct fields, two conditional spec keys, and - critically - the hand-written map path in findingsFromList, because this action decodes findings twice and the native-list path is the only one this feature uses. Absent -> both keys omitted -> byte-identical to today for every other producer. No validation or evaluation happens here by design: that is the gate job, upstream, and a producer without the gate step can never populate these fields.

One registry entry, beside verify_cited_cardinals and verify_report_prose. This is also what the migration _HOLD depends on: a step naming an action the binary does not register is rejected whole with requires a topic, so this must be in a rolled image before the config lands.
edits.sketch:
"verify_cited_cardinals": {
 		Handler:     VerifyCitedCardinalsAction,
 		Category:    "validation",
 		IsLocal:     true,
 	},
+	"verify_acceptance_predicates": {
+		Handler:     VerifyAcceptancePredicatesAction,
+		Category:    "validation",
+		Description: "Deterministic gate on a finding optional machine-checkable acceptance predicate: refute-only, and kept only where it already refutes the page as it stands (features_open/030 v2(d))",
+		IsLocal:     true,
+	},

edits.rationale: The config half: insert the gate step, rewire the chain, and tell the model the contract. _HOLD because config is live on apply and Go is not (537 precedent; 49 items elsewhere were stamped complete carrying a WORKFLOW_INVALID that proved nothing ran). The target row is resolved ONCE into a temp table so gate and writes are the same set by construction - 537 guardian-seat finding that four agent types carry two active rows while only the higher version is loaded. The prompt anchor is asserted to occur EXACTLY ONCE before anything is written. The contract is deliberately NOT added to the OUTPUT skeleton, because every key there reads as required and this one must default to absent - and the verify block asserts that ABSENCE by counting occurrences, which is the half a verify block usually forgets. The full anchor sentence is elided in this sketch only to keep the JSON quoting sane; it is verbatim in the file.
